deep.reconstruction:
This page continues a self-contained development of the Schatten–von Neumann classes L^p(H) of compact operators. The previous page proved 'lemma 1' by induction on n, using the squaring trick ||AB||_{2^{n-1}}^{2^{n-1}} = Tr (ABB*A*)^{2^{n-2}}. Lemma 1 is the generalized Hölder inequality for 2^n equal exponents: ||A_1…A_N||_1 ≤ ∏||A_i||_N with N = 2^n.

Part 2) proves the Hölder inequality ||AB||_1 ≤ ||A||_p ||B||_q for 1/p + 1/q = 1.
- Reduction: by density it suffices to treat A, B trace class (indeed finite rank would do).
- Polar decompositions: write A = UH and B = KV with U, V partial isometries, H = |A| and K = |B*|. Then ||AB||_1 ≤ ||HK||_1.
- Dyadic splitting: for α + β = 2^n, set h = H^{1/α} and k = K^{1/β}. Then HK = h^α k^β is a product of 2^n factors.
- Lemma 1 then gives ||HK||_1 ≤ ||h||_{2^n}^α ||k||_{2^n}^β = (Tr H^λ)^{1/λ} (Tr K^μ)^{1/μ}, where λ = 2^n/α and μ = 2^n/β.
- So Hölder holds for every conjugate pair (λ, μ) whose reciprocals are dyadic rationals. Continuity in the exponent extends it to all conjugate pairs (p, p').
- A marginal note says the same argument gives the n-fold version: ||A_1…A_n||_1 ≤ ∏||A_i||_{p_i} when Σ 1/p_i = 1.

Part 3) draws the consequences:
- the duality formula ||A||_p = sup_{||B||_{p'} ≤ 1} |Tr AB|;
- hence the Minkowski (triangle) inequality, so ||·||_p is a norm;
- the general Hölder ||AB||_r ≤ ||A||_p ||B||_q whenever 1/p + 1/q ≥ 1/r, using monotonicity of the Schatten norms.

The purpose shows on the next page. Grothendieck uses these inequalities, together with exterior powers ΛA, to bound the quantities α_m of singular values (traces of exterior powers). That points to Fredholm-determinant estimates for his theory of nuclear/Fredholm operators (1953–56).
errors: Slip in the final displayed inequality: it reads (Tr H^p)^{1/p}(Tr H^{p'})^{1/p'}; the second factor should be K^{p'} (and one uses ||K||_{p'} = ||B||_{p'} since |B*| and |B| have the same singular values).

The passage to the limit in the exponent is called 'immédiat'. It requires continuity of p ↦ (Tr H^p)^{1/p}, which is fine for trace-class or finite-rank H, but is left unstated. The endpoint case p = 1, q = ∞ is not covered by the dyadic argument (it needs α, β ≥ 1) but is trivial.
The reduction 'on peut supposer A, B ∈ L^1' tacitly uses density plus continuity of both sides; this is not justified on the page.

ideas.what: Hölder inequality for Schatten classes, ||AB||_1 ≤ ||A||_p||B||_q, and its n-fold version
ideas.modern_name: Hölder inequality for Schatten–von Neumann ideals
ideas.usually_credited_to: von Neumann, Schatten (1940s); Dixmier (1953) for semifinite von Neumann algebras
ideas.where_published: Possibly used in 'Produits tensoriels topologiques' (1955) / 'La théorie de Fredholm' (1956); not verified

ideas.what: Proof via dyadic exponents: equal-exponent 2^n case by squaring/induction, then splitting H = h^α with α + β = 2^n, then density of dyadic rationals
ideas.modern_name: Dyadic interpolation / 'tensor-power trick'-style proof of Hölder
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard technique (cf. Simon, Trace Ideals; Gohberg–Krein)

ideas.what: Duality ||A||_p = sup |Tr AB| over the unit ball of L^{p'}, giving the triangle inequality
ideas.modern_name: Duality L^p ↔ L^{p'} of Schatten classes

deep.surprise_reason: A clean but standard re-derivation of Hölder and Minkowski for Schatten classes via a dyadic induction. This was already known by 1953 (Schatten–von Neumann, Dixmier). The only mildly notable feature is the elementary dyadic route and its link (next page) to exterior-power estimates for Fredholm theory.
transcription_corrections: Final displayed inequality: the manuscript indeed reads 'Tr H^{p'}' (author's slip for K^{p'}); the transcription is faithful but this should be flagged.
The arrowed marginal line reads roughly: 'Le même argument montre que si 1/p_1 + 1/p_2 + … + 1/p_n = 1, ||A_1…A_n||_1 ≤ ||A_1||_{p_1} … ||A_n||_{p_n}'.

'Cette inégalité est vraie pour (λ, μ > 1) pourvu qu'on puisse les mettre sous la forme 2^n/α, 2^n/β avec α + β = 2^n, i.e. pourvu que 1/λ + 1/μ = 1 et que 1/λ et 1/μ soient multiples de 1/2^n; par passage à la limite immédiat, on conclut' — plausible reading of the middle paragraph.
